answer: Every identity stores one 2 TB ridge of a shared dataset, hashed and pinned, and a cluster of n sits on terrace n, so each member holds 2n TB. Each epoch, random falcon probes demand a 1 MB slice from a random terrace in 30 seconds. Twelve rotating checkers verify each hash before the epoch closes. One missed slice voids the shard, burns the identity, and drops its cluster off the ridge. 100 clones need 20,000 TB of drives, about $1,000,000 at $50 per TB; one honest agent pays $100 for a single ridge. That bill turns a clone farm into a warehouse renting a hundred lockers to hide one key.
